summary: The diff implements parseFloat steps 1-7 in order. ToString and TrimString(start) are called on the argument, and the prefix scan follows the StrDecimalLiteral grammar: optional sign, then Infinity, or DecimalDigits with optional '.' and fraction, then an optional exponent that is only consumed when complete. A lone '.' or sign with no digits returns NaN, and "-" applies to the magnitude so -0 comes out right. No test-shaped branches or hardcoded results. The only oddities are harmless: `?` where the spec uses `!` on TrimString (which cannot throw here), and an unreachable `unwrap_or(NaN)` on a parse of a well-formed string.
notes_for_next_attempt: No defects found. The change can be merged as is. Optional cleanup only: the `.unwrap_or(f64::NAN)` after parsing the constructed float literal is unreachable for well-formed input and could be dropped or documented. Also, the step 2 `?` on trim_string could be `!` to match the spec, though this has no observable effect.
